notes:
- The cover viewer is a gallery now: LiveChart's own `/visuals` tab is read after the search page, so every key visual and character visual becomes a swipeable page with a `2 / 4` counter and a save button that saves the image on screen. The poster and banner still paint first; a title with no visuals falls back to its LiveChart poster.
- The docked title bar is centred and legible: the title takes the space the actions do not use, is centred inside its pill, and the old progress wash - a rectangle clipped by the capsule that cut through the title - is a 3dp rounded line along the bottom edge.
- Activity cards show the show's banner: the feed used to blow up the 2:3 cover and blur it, which made every row the same smudge. It now requests AniList's wide `bannerImage`, draws it sharp under a bottom-weighted scrim, and keeps the cover only as a faint fallback for titles with no banner.
- Retention has a strength, not just a switch: Subtle keeps the show's colour in the accent and buttons while the palette keeps the background, Balanced eases the tint halfway, and Full keeps the scheme the sheet was drawn with. The sheet itself is always full tint; Reset appearance still takes the colour back.
- Filter the dashboard by episode count: the filter sheet gained Any, 1+, 6+, 12+ and 24+ beside the minimum rating, following the same rule as the score floor - a title with no announced length drops out while a minimum is set. The quick filter bar restates it and clearing filters clears it.
- Settings and Info read more clearly: version, package and data source share one grouped surface with dividers, package ids centre against their label, section titles match the shelf rows, and Info cards are more opaque and spaced further apart so a retained tint cannot read through a paragraph.
- A kept colour now keeps its background: Retaining a cover colour used to stop at the accent - the sheet closed and every surface snapped back to the palette's navy while only the buttons kept the show's hue, which read as the colour being lost at the moment it was meant to be kept. The stored colour builds the tinted scheme now, so the background survives the sheet, page changes and the next launch; a palette, a hue or Reset appearance still takes it back.
- The progress wave reads as a progress bar: The Watching Progress card at zero episodes was a faint squiggle with nothing above it. The track is legible on a dark surface, the fill keeps a round start marker at 0%, the card says Not started yet under the wave, and the entrance is keyed on the title so a relation opens at zero instead of arriving full.
- LiveChart's poster actually loads: The scrape read only `src`, so a lazily loaded search page - real URL in a data attribute, placeholder in `src` - produced no cover and no pill. It reads whichever attribute carries the poster, takes the smallest `srcset` variant, upgrades protocol-relative URLs, swaps the size segment on any format, and shares one in-flight fetch per title.
- The cover viewer switches instead of cutting: Sources crossfade, the close fades and shrinks before the dialog goes (the written exit had never run), a stale source index is clamped instead of drawing an empty frame, and the source pills stay on one line when the LiveChart cover arrives.
- A received message knows when it arrived: Received rows kept only the embedded message's timestamp, so an empty one printed no age and sorted behind every sent message however old. The notification's own timestamp is the fallback, so the row's time and its place in the list are both right.
- Thirty-three more ways it ended: The dark tone grows - the finale's most quoted line improvised the day the actor learned the show was ending, the sequel announced on April Fools' and never denied, the 4K remaster that found detail in the background and none in the ending.
